claims.text: Put \(A_{r,q}:=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\). The actual interval ideals are \[ J_v=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda,\qquad J_{v^\vee}=\bigoplus_{j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq r^q}\mathbb Z\bar s_\nu . \] Indeed, each displayed interval span contains the respective source-given generators. LR containment makes it an ideal, since every surviving product term still contains the lower rectangle. Hence it contains the generated ideal; conversely its basis elements are generators, giving equality. The quotient Schur basis makes both sums direct.

Assume \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) is bigrassmannian: \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\). Let \(q=n-r\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), and \[ v^\vee:=v_{q,n-s,q-s+t,n}=v_{q,q-i+j,q-i+1,n}. \] Then \(i,j\ge1\), \(q-i=t-(r+s-n)-1\ge0\), and \(r-j=t-1\ge0\). Thus \(q\ge1\), \(1\le t^\vee=q-i+1\le q\), and \[ t^\vee\le n-s\iff t\le r. \] Therefore \(1\le t^\vee\le r^\vee=q,s^\vee=n-s\le n\), and \[ t^\vee-(r^\vee+s^\vee-n) =(q-i+1)-(q-s)=t>0. \] Hence \(v^\vee\) is bigrassmannian. Its parameters satisfy \[ i^\vee=j,\quad j^\vee=i,\quad a^\vee=\min(r-j,q-i)=a,\quad b^\vee=\min(j,i)=b. \]

The integral Schur involution \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution of \(\Lambda\). Since \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q\), it sends \(I_{r,q}\) onto \(I_{q,r}\), inducing \[ \bar\omega:A_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{q,r}. \] Moreover \(i^j\subseteq\lambda\iff j^i\subseteq\lambda'\); hence \(\bar\omega\) bijects the two displayed interval Schur bases and \[ \bar\omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}. \]

Theorem 1.2 applies to every bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), defines \(i,j,a,b\) as above, and states minimality of \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) in the integral quotient. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 68-78] [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 95-110]

claims.text: Applying Theorem 1.2 to \(v^\vee\) gives a minimal generating family bounded above by \((j^i,b^a)\). Since \[ (j^i,b^a)'=((i+a)^b,i^{\,j-b}), \] its pullback under \(\bar\omega^{-1}\) is \[ \{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}. \] Ring isomorphisms preserve generation and minimality: a proper generating subfamily after pullback would map to a proper generating subfamily before pullback. This includes \(a=0\), with empty blocks omitted.
